sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- UKMTO] An incident occurred ~25 nm NE of Khasab: crew safe, fire extinguished, vessel continuing its journey; UKMTO did not name the vessel. [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- Reuters via 3 maritime sources, relayed by NDTV/Oneindia/ABP/gCaptain/Bloomberg] The vessel was MT Louise 1; a small boat attached two limpet mines to its hull; detonations caused an engine-room fire and temporarily disabled the tanker; this is the first successful limpet-mine strike in Hormuz since the US-Iran war began in February 2026 (a September attempt failed to detonate). [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- Indian minister] All 27 Indian seafarers aboard safe, no injuries; Arzanah (2 Indians) also safe. [UNVERIFIED] Attacker identity: no claimant, no attribution in any cited source -- any narration naming Iran as the attacker exceeds the sources. COUNTERPOINT: UKMTO's own advisory names no vessel and no weapon; the limpet identification rests on unnamed maritime sources, not on UKMTO. PortWatch backbone: newest snapshot remains portwatch-2026-10-26.json (observation 2026-10-18, Hormuz 4 transits, 7-day avg 3.7 vs 2025 baseline 85.5/day, stale=true) -- counted figure WITHHELD as live, cited only as stale.
sections.what_verified: UKMTO advisory + Reuters wire + minister statement converge on the incident; vessel identification and limpet method rest on Reuters' unnamed maritime sources relayed by multiple outlets
sections.what_disputed: UKMTO advisory itself names no vessel and no weapon type; attacker unidentified in every cited source; dating differs (Oct 29 vs Oct 30) across relays.
sections.why_matters: The new weapon in Hormuz: 2 magnetic mines, 1 small boat, 0 attribution -- the first limpet strike of the war.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (Oct 29-30 event, absent from all prior Nov 1 scans; surfaced in-window via Nov 1 relays) -- MT Louise 1, Panama-flagged crude tanker, hit by two limpet mines attached by a small boat ~25 nm NE of Khasab, Oman; engine-room fire, vessel temporarily disabled, crew safe, voyage resumed; first successful limpet-mine strike of the US-Iran war (Feb 2026-); attacker NOT identified

The fault line our audience is arguing over: Can any navy stop a small boat with magnetic mines in the world's narrowest oil chokepoint -- or is every tanker now exposed?
